title: Recording: When The Wind Is Blowing by Paul McCartney | 1971
content:
Studio A-1, A&R Recording, New York City
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Dixon Van Winkle

Paul McCartney worked on the unreleased track ‘When The Wind Is Blowing’ on 22 January 1971.

‘When The Wind Is Blowing’ was written by McCartney in 1969. It was inspired by a print of Picasso’s ‘The Old Guitarist’, that McCartney saw hanging in the Avenue Clinic in north London when his daughter Mary was born.

The backing track had been recorded during the early Ram sessions on 20 October 1970.

The song initially had the working title ‘Rupert’, and was earmarked for a mooted Rupert the Bear animation, and an early version was recorded during the sessions for the McCartney album. Wings recorded another version in 1978.

On this day Paul and Linda McCartney added a single vocal take, using a shared microphone. The song had no lyrics apart from the title, so they mostly sang wordless melodies, with harmonies during the verses.
